name: Shri Balaji Restaurant
why_it_matters: The dosa institution of downtown Rishikesh — locals send pilgrims here when they're tired of north-Indian thalis. Same Mayakund corner since 1987, prices that haven't tracked Tapovan inflation.
insider_tip: Skip the south-Indian thali and order the butter masala dosa with extra coconut chutney; the chef's been making it the same way for three decades.
signature_address: 17 Ghat Road, Mayakund, Near Triveni Ghat, Rishikesh 249201

name: Pappu Lassi
why_it_matters: Tucked into the bazaar lane that feeds into Triveni Ghat — clay-pot lassi served thick enough to chew. Open since 1995, run by the namesake family, and far more hygienic than the typical pilgrim-stand variety.
insider_tip: Order the namkeen (cumin-salt) variant — it's what the locals drink after the morning ghat dip; the sweet versions get heavy after a kachori breakfast.
signature_address: Ghat Road, Near Triveni Ghat, Manvendera Nagar, Rishikesh 249201

name: Rajasthani Mishthan Bhandar
why_it_matters: Triveni Ghat Chowk's go-to sweet-and-thali stop — the only spot near the ghat with a respectable Rajasthani thali, freshly fried kachori-jalebi mornings, and ghevar in season. Constant pilgrim traffic, glass-counter sweets up front, dining hall at the back.
insider_tip: Eat the kachori-jalebi combo before 11am while it's fresh from the kadhai; afternoon batches sit in the trays. The thali is unlimited refills if you ask.
signature_address: Haridwar Road, Triveni Ghat Chowk, Manvendera Nagar, Rishikesh 249201

name: Daana Paani
why_it_matters: Unlimited Punjabi thali a hundred metres from the aarti steps — the lunch default for families coming off the morning Ganga dip. Plain canteen-style room, fast turnover, no surprises.
insider_tip: The thali is the value play; à-la-carte mains are ordinary. Refills on dal, sabzi and roti are unlimited — pace yourself or you'll skip the aarti.
signature_address: 1 Ghat Road, Near Triveni Ghat, Rishikesh 249201

name: Bikaneri Gali
why_it_matters: Larger family-restaurant on the Dehradun Road approach to Triveni — tour-bus groups stop here for thali plus a sweet counter on the way out. Air-conditioned hall, big-group friendly, the kind of place locals book for small functions.
insider_tip: Skip the indo-Chinese; order the Rajasthani thali and walk out with a box of pista barfi from the front counter — that's what the regulars do.
signature_address: Dehradun Road, Tirah, Near City Centre, Rishikesh 249201

name: Krishna Misthan Bhandar
why_it_matters: Family-run sweet shop and dining hall on Haridwar Road since 1985 — pilgrim-priced thalis, glass-counter mithai up front, hot jalebi at the door in the evenings. Often packed; service is brisk rather than warm.
insider_tip: Buy a quarter-kilo of jalebi-rabri from the takeaway counter, eat it on the ghat steps after sundown — the dine-in hall is functional but the food is the point.
signature_address: Haridwar Road, Near Triveni Ghat, Mayakund, Rishikesh 249201

name: Agra Sweet
why_it_matters: One of the older sweet-and-snack counters in the main city, on Tilak Road close to the bus stand. Mornings are kachori-subzi and jalebi; evenings turn into a samosa-pakora rush as office crowds head home.
insider_tip: Mornings are when this place earns its reputation — arrive by 9am for hot kachori with cold jalebi. By afternoon the snacks are reheated.
signature_address: 145, Tilak Road, Bankhandi, Doctor Colony, Rishikesh 249201

name: Deepak Hotel Rishikesh
signature_dish: yellow dal fry with stuffed parantha
why_it_matters: Working dhaba next to the old roadways bus stand on Tilak Road — where drivers, conductors and early-morning bus passengers eat. Plastic chairs, fast service, parantha-and-dal that hasn't changed in decades.
insider_tip: Order whatever is sitting on the tava at the entrance — turnover is so quick that the freshest dish is whatever's being made when you walk in. Cash only.
signature_address: Tilak Road, Near Old Roadways Bus Stand, Rishikesh 249201
